Playbook.name: AD — Group Policy Object Modified by an Unexpected Principal - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A groupPolicyContainer object was modified (5136) - GPO changes push configuration/scripts to many machines at once. Triage question: was this a sanctioned change by a GPO administrator, or an unexpected principal editing policy (a fast route to mass code execution/persistence)?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A single malicious GPO edit can deploy scheduled tasks, scripts, or privilege changes to every machine in an OU - bank-wide impact from one change.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: GPO object change
Signal.Details: 5136 where ObjectClass is groupPolicyContainer (new_terms on the principal).

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: DC where the change was recorded.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Recognised GPO admin during a change window: verify ticket, likely benign.
Unexpected principal (new_terms fired because this actor never edits GPOs) editing policy: escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether $username is an authorised GPO administrator and whether the change is limited/expected.

Step.name: Scope the GPO change activity by this principal
Step.Purpose: How many GPO attributes/objects the principal touched signals routine edit vs broad tampering.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("5136","5137","5141") AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.ObjectDN, winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName, event.code | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 40
Step.AnalystNotes: Look at which GPOs and attributes changed. gPCMachineExtensionNames / versionNumber edits accompany real policy changes; edits to many GPOs at once is concerning.

Step.name: Is this principal a habitual GPO editor
Step.Purpose: new_terms fired because the (principal) is new to this action - confirm whether they have any legitimate directory-admin footprint.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("5136","4728","4732","4756","4738") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS ops = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A principal simultaneously editing GPOs AND changing group memberships is acting like an attacker consolidating control.

Step.name: Actor's session origin
Step.Purpose: Locate where the actor is operating from for containment and to spot foothold-driven changes.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND event.code == "4624" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: An admin editing GPOs from their normal admin workstation is expected; edits driven from an unusual host point to a compromised session.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the principal has no legitimate directory-admin footprint, or is concurrently changing groups/rights.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised GPO Tampering - IR, review GPO contents)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows edits to logon/startup script or scheduled-task policy extensions by an unexpected principal.
INV-01/02 show a recognised GPO admin making a scoped change during an approved window with a ticket.
Principal is plausibly delegated but no change record and change scope is broad.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-GPO-CHANGE, INV-02-GPO-ACTOR, INV-03-GPO-SESSION to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Sanctioned GPO administration by an authorised admin.

Indicators.Item: Actor is a known GPO/OU admin.
Edit is scoped to the intended GPO.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change ticket and GPO diff.

TruePositive.Definition: Unauthorised policy modification to deploy code or persistence domain-wide.

Indicators.Item: Actor also altering groups/rights or operating from an unusual host.

SOCAction.Item: Review the modified GPO's contents immediately; revert unauthorised changes.
Disable the actor, isolate its host, open IR.
Check which OUs/machines the GPO applies to for blast radius.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A configuration-management tool editing GPOs unexpectedly due to misconfiguration.

Indicators.Item: A known automation account making the change per a broken/new job.

SOCAction.Item: Correct the automation scope; document the expected principal so new_terms stops firing.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Pull the modified GPO contents; revert if unauthorised.
Disable actor and isolate its host if suspicious.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Determine blast radius (linked OUs/machines); hunt for deployed tasks/scripts on clients.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict GPO edit rights; enable GPO change approval; back up GPOs for rapid diff/restore.

QualityChecks.Check: ObjectClass groupPolicyContainer confirmed; new_terms keys on principal - expected admins will each fire once then be learned.
Consider pairing with SYSVOL file-change monitoring for script payloads.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised admin + ticket + scoped GPO diff confirmed benign.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Malicious GPO reverted; blast radius cleaned; actor eradicated.
